subject: Next steps & prompt collection: Searchly model-fit follow-up
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@searchly.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@searchly.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps & prompt collection: Searchly model-fit follow-up

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the Searchly team and hear more about the extractor + QA use cases you outlined. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Shared context: production search enrichment pipeline, mixed short/long prompts (query-level + 3–5 doc context), high-precision requirements for entity redaction, and occasional latency spikes during peak indexing jobs.
- Primary goals: baseline quality parity with current transformer ensemble, reduce per-token cost by ~35% vs current deployed endpoint, and a safe rollout path for PII redaction.

Recommended immediate next steps:
1) Collect a representative prompt set from you (100–300 examples) including the edge cases you mentioned (multi-lingual snippets, heavily truncated docs, and synthetic noisy OCR). Use the CSV template attached — three columns: id, prompt, expected_output (redacted/output format).
2) We’ll run a focused model-fit eval on two candidate variants: redwood-13b-instruct-quant (fast/cheap) and redwood-70b-rw-qlora (high-quality fallback). I’ll share benchmark links and a short eval plan.
3) Safety/redaction: please flag any prompts that must be redacted in training/benchmarking exports; we’ll treat those as PII-only and run local-only evaluations if needed.

Attachments: searchly-prompt-examples.csv (CSV template), model-fit-benchmarks-2026-03.pdf (pilot plan + sample results from similar customers)

Could you drop the sample CSV into this thread by EOD Friday PST? If the 300-example ask is heavy, please send a prioritized 50–100 subset that captures the worst failure modes.

I’ll loop in Monica (SE) and Vivek (solutions) on the follow-up eval and redaction guidance.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@searchly.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@searchly.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & prompt collection: Searchly model-fit follow-up

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the summary — that matches our notes. Attaching a first-pass CSV with 112 rows (called Searchly_sample_prompts_v1.csv). It includes:
- 80 production-derived prompts (query + 2–3 doc context snippets)
- 20 OCR-noisy examples (from last month’s ingestion)
- 12 multi-lingual edge cases (en/es/pt)

A few important flags in the "expected_output" column: where PII redaction is required we put [REDACTED] and added a column "redaction_level" with values HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW. We’re nervous about hallucination on truncated docs (one of our biggest 2nd-order failures), and the latency during concurrent indexing windows.

Questions:
1) For the two candidate models you proposed, can you share expected latency per token at 512-context and estimated cost delta vs our current endpoint?
2) We need guidance on how you handle prompt-level redaction before sending examples to any hosted evals — can you confirm local-only processing options?

Attaching: Searchly_sample_prompts_v1.csv (CSV, 112 rows)

—Elena
Sr. Product Manager, Searchly
elena.morales@searchly.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@searchly.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & prompt collection: Searchly model-fit follow-up

Elena — great, got the file and appreciate the redaction flags. Quick answers and plan: 

1) Latency & cost (back-of-envelope for 512 tokens; will refine after we profile your actual sequence-length distribution):
   - redwood-13b-instruct-quant: median p95 latency ~ 120–160ms/token on a T4-equivalent dedicated backend; estimated unit cost ~ $0.006 / 1k tokens (pilot pricing). Good candidate for bulk requests where strict 100% parity isn’t required.
   - redwood-70b-rw-qlora: median p95 latency ~ 60–90ms/token on A100-class; estimated unit cost ~ $0.025 / 1k tokens. Best for high-precision routes and can be used as a canary/fallback for critical queries.

2) Redaction & local-only processing:
   - Short answer: yes. We can run the initial evals in your VPC/private deployment or via a local-only eval flow. Options:
     a) Private eval: you deploy our private eval container into your VPC; samples never leave your network.
     b) PII-stripping preprocessor: we can accept your CSV and run a configured redaction pass (based on your redaction_level column) on our side, returning a redacted version and explicit mapping file to you; we only store the redacted artifact in our ephemeral eval environment and delete it after 14 days.

Plan: Monica will scope the eval (metrics: exact-match redaction, hallucination rate on truncated docs, token-cost/latency). Vivek will run an initial cost/throughput projection and suggest batching/cache settings to reduce unit cost during batch enrichment.

Links for reference:
- Pilot benchmark framework: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-searchly-benchmarks
- Example eval results (customer anonymized): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1x9y-example-benchmarks

Next steps we need from you:
- Final CSV upload (if you want us to run the private eval, mark REDACT_PRIV in the subject and we’ll start the private flow).
- Any sequence-length stats you can share (p95 token length) — or we can sample from your CSV.

I’ve attached a short one-pager with the eval metric definitions.

Thanks —
Karthik

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & prompt collection: Searchly model-fit follow-up

Elena / team —

Thanks for the sample CSV, Elena — good coverage. A few immediate asks so our eval produces actionable outputs: 

1) Please add a column called "priority_flags" if possible with tags like: MUST_REDACT, CAN_USE_AS_IS, FALLBACK_TEST. That helps us segment the eval (safety vs quality).
2) For each example you marked as HIGH redaction_level, can you add a short note in the CSV describing why — e.g., contains SSN, contains full-name+email, or contains internal-only keys. That tells our redaction heuristics which regexes to prioritize.
3) If you can, please include 10–15 negative examples where the expected output is an empty/NO_HIT result — these help calibrate hallucination thresholds.

What we’ll deliver after the pilot run (7 business days after we receive the final CSV and access mode):
- Evaluation report (precision/recall for redaction, hallucination rate on truncated docs, per-model latency/cost)
- Suggested routing policy: primary route to 13b-quant, fallback to 70b-qlora for low-confidence outputs or flagged MUST_REDACT cases
- Prompt hygiene guide with example transformations to reduce hallucination on truncated contexts

If you want the private eval, reply with subject prefix REDACT_PRIV and we’ll send the private-container deployment instructions.

Thanks —
Monica
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
